full_translation_en:
Parliament
National Assembly
Complete Verbatim Report of the 21st Session
September 9, 2083
Wednesday
Meeting Number: 42
The meeting commenced today at 10:19 AM under the chairmanship of the Right Honourable Speaker, Mr. Narayan Prasad Dahal.
(10:19 AM)
Right Honourable Speaker: Honourable members of the National Assembly, the meeting begins. Honourable members, I will provide time for those who have registered to speak during the Zero Hour.
First, Honourable Member Khamma Bahadur Khati.
Honourable Mr. Khamma Bahadur Khati (Nepali Congress): Honourable Speaker,
In Matri, Bajura district, there has been a lack of specialist doctors, causing hardship and difficulty for the public, and their economic situation is not strong. As a result, the people there are being deprived of health services. Therefore, I would like to draw the attention of the government through the Honourable Speaker to prioritize Bajura district and provide specialist doctors.
Right Honourable Speaker: Honourable Member Gita Devkota.
(10:20 AM)
Honourable Ms. Gita Devkota (Nepali Congress): Honourable Speaker,
Where is the country heading? From innocent 3-year-old girls to daughters from fathers, they are unsafe. The horrific rapes, violence, and murders happening daily have bowed humanity's head. The nation's dignity has been tarnished. The declining standard of moral education and the lack of practical sex education have spread perversion. The leniency of the law and the indifferent administration have emboldened criminals. Empty consolation from the government is no longer enough. I strongly urge the government to implement mandatory moral and practical sex education in schools, expedite the process for child sexual violence cases with fast-track courts and the strictest possible punishment, and for the state to immediately protect citizens' safety and social and moral values. (Time expired.)
Right Honourable Speaker: Honourable Member Jagat Timilsina.
(10:21 AM)
Honourable Mr. Jagat Timilsina (Nepali Congress): Honourable Speaker,
A serious question needs to be raised about the government's approach to sensitive issues like Nepal's foreign policy and diplomatic representation. An ambassador is a representative of the state, government, and national interest. Out of the 31 Nepali embassies in various countries, 21 are without ambassadors. Important missions have been operating on an acting basis for a long time. This is not a mere administrative delay; it is a serious gamble with Nepal's diplomatic capacity. Honourable Speaker, diplomacy today is not just about formal meetings, banquets, and diplomatic receptions. This is the era of digital diplomacy, economic diplomacy, bringing in investment, technology transfer, expanding trade, protecting the interests of Nepali workers, and gaining influence in the international market. Through the Honourable Speaker, my question to the government is, is this bill a priority for the government? If not... (Time expired.)
Right Honourable Speaker: Honourable Member Dharmendra Paswan.
(10:22 AM)
Honourable Mr. Dharmendra Paswan (Nepali Congress): Honourable Speaker,
In Rautahat, a person died from a snakebite due to a vaccine. Also, the embankments on both sides of the Lalbakaiya River in Rautahat, in wards 3, 1, and 2 of Paroha Municipality, are on the verge of breaking. Due to the government's lack of concern, there is a possibility of 1,000 households being displaced if it breaks. I request that immediate action be taken through this house. Also, regarding the incident involving Garima Chaudhary, immediate action must be taken. I see it being politicized, so I believe immediate action should be taken. Thank you.
Right Honourable Speaker: Honourable Member Mahanta Thakur.
(10:23 AM)
Honourable Mr. Mahanta Thakur (Democratic Socialist Party, Nepal):
(Sound not heard.)
Right Honourable Speaker: Honourable Member Meenasingh Rakhal.
(10:24 AM)
Honourable Ms. Meenasingh Rakhal (Communist Party of Nepal, UML): Honourable Speaker, violence against women and children in Nepal is becoming a serious challenge. According to Nepal Police, in the first six months of the current fiscal year, 8,214 people were victims of domestic violence, of whom 7,401 are women. Cybercrime complaints have also reached 20,526 in one year. What is even more worrying is that heinous crimes like murder after rape are also occurring. Therefore, the question is not just whether the law exists, but whether the law is effective. The government must be serious about the strict implementation of existing laws, enacting clear laws that cover new forms of cyber violence, immediate protection for victims, swift investigation, and timely justice. Justice should be felt by the victim, not just exist on paper. Thank you.
Right Honourable Speaker: Honourable Member Ranjit Karna.
(10:26 AM)
Honourable Mr. Ranjit Karna (Nepali Congress): Honourable Speaker,
In Rajbiraj Municipality, Nepal's first planned city, the movement for land ownership by 52,000 households some time ago resulted in an agreement from the Nepal government to distribute land ownership certificates, but a long time has passed. No concrete process has been initiated yet. Similarly, regarding the Rajbiraj-Bhardah road section, despite the commitment to terminate the previous contractor's contract and award a new one, no tendering process has moved forward yet. Furthermore, what is sad is that a few days ago, the Honourable Health Minister inspected the Gajendra Narayan Singh Hospital in Rajbiraj. Despite the shortage of beds, patients were being treated on the floor in a dramatic fashion, but after the minister left, they were treated on the floor. Therefore, I draw your attention to the need for bed arrangements and action against the concerned staff. Thank you.
Right Honourable Speaker: Honourable Member Ms. Rekha Kumari Jha.
(10:27 AM)
Honourable Ms. Rekha Kumari Jha (Communist Party of Nepal, UML): Honourable Speaker, the number of deaths of pregnant women due to the lack of skilled doctors in provincial hospitals is increasing. In particular, the death rate of pregnant women is high in the Provincial Hospital in Janakpur. The negligence of the doctors here is evident. They spend more time in their own clinics and show no responsibility towards government institutions. As a result, the public has protested multiple times with slogans, rallies, and even blockades. This has been raised through the media and newspapers repeatedly. I urge the government to pay attention to this as well. Finally, I want to say that the government, not the law, but the public should punish the perpetrator of the crime against the girl named Garima... (Time expired.)
Right Honourable Speaker: Honourable Member Ms. Roshni Mechhe.
(10:28 AM)
Honourable Ms. Roshni Mechhe (Communist Party of Nepal, UML): Honourable Speaker, the increasing heinous crimes of rape and the slow justice system in the country raise serious questions about the state's presence. The horrific incident of the rape and murder of 3-year-old Garima Chaudhary in Bara has shocked the entire nation. Will citizens feel safe just by building four-sided structures on street corners? Justice should be ensured immediately through fast-track courts and necessary amendments to the law to prevent such heinous crimes from recurring. Furthermore, the Ministry of Health appears insensitive and silent even as citizens are dying from Japanese encephalitis in Jhapa. Similarly, Ramesh Mechhe from Mechinagar, Jhapa, who lost his life while working abroad in Saudi Arabia, his body has not been brought back to the country for 20 days, leaving his elderly parents and family in grief and pain for a long time. I urge the government to take immediate concrete steps by diplomatic efforts to expedite the repatriation of the body and address all these serious issues. Thank you.
Right Honourable Speaker: Honourable Member Mr. Basudev Ghimire.
(10:29 AM)
Honourable Mr. Basudev Ghimire (Nepali Congress): Honourable Speaker,
Basanta Kalathoki from Ward No. 17 of Ghorahi, Dang district, died due to a physical assault at a hostel in Kathmandu. Upon hearing the news of his death, his mother also died by suicide. I express my condolences to both mother and son and extend my sympathies to the bereaved family. I urge the Nepal government through the Honourable Speaker to immediately investigate the cause of Basanta Kalathoki's death and take strict action against the culprits. Thank you, Jai Nepal.
Right Honourable Speaker: Honourable Member Ms. Samjhana Devkota.
(10:30 AM)
Honourable Ms. Samjhana Devkota (Communist Party of Nepal, UML): Honourable Speaker, women are unsafe everywhere today. Looking at the data from the last 4 years, more than 250 women and children are raped every year. We see that even more children under 10 years old are being raped, the data shows this. I believe that the increase in rape cases this year is also due to our lack of moral education and inability to control cybercrime. In such a situation, not only children but the entire family is broken. I am also shocked by the statement made by the former Deputy Speaker on such a serious matter. Where will this take the entire country? We need not only laws but also strict punishment. Thank you.
Right Honourable Speaker: Honourable Member Mr. Somnath Poudel.
(10:31 AM)
Honourable Mr. Somnath Poudel (Communist Party of Nepal, UML): Honourable Speaker, the brutal murder of 3-year-old innocent girl Garima Chaudhary after rape has plunged Nepali society into grief and pain. It should be our goal to speak out for Garima's justice. However, what has been seen is an unprecedented display of inhuman, insensitive, primitive, semi-conscious behaviour. On one hand, the Home Minister is filming videos in Singha Durbar, and on the other hand, videos are being filmed under police direction. The intent and dialogue in both these incidents are so ugly, heartbreaking, and horrific that it is difficult to even imagine. The parents of the murdered girl are made to say 'we are happy,' while the accused are allowed to boast and declare victory. I urge the government not to turn the citizens' pain into a spectacle. Thank you.
Right Honourable Speaker: Honourable members, the Zero Hour speaking session
(10:32 AM)
concludes. Honourable members, I now provide time for the Honourable Minister for Law, Justice, and Parliamentary Affairs, Sovita Gautam, to present a proposal to send the Bill Relating to the Reinstatement of Provisions of the Nepal Special Service Act, 2042, received with a message from the House of Representatives, to the Legislation Management Committee for clause-wise discussion, on behalf of the Right Honourable Prime Minister Balendra Shah.
Honourable Minister for Law, Justice, and Parliamentary Affairs, Ms. Sovita Gautam: Honourable Speaker, with the permission of the Honourable Speaker, the Bill Relating to the Reinstatement of Provisions of the Nepal Special Service Act, 2042, received with a message from the House of Representatives...

I present before this esteemed assembly the proposal that the Nepal Special Service Act, 2042 (Amendment) Bill, 2083, sent with a message from the House of Representatives, be sent to the Legislation Management Committee for clause-by-clause discussion. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable members, now, the proposal that the Nepal Special Service Act, 2042 (Amendment) Bill, 2083, sent with a message from the House of Representatives, be sent to the Legislation Management Committee for clause-by-clause discussion, is presented for decision. Honorable members in favor of this proposal will say "Yes" and honorable members against it will say "No". Honorable members in favor of this proposal say "Yes". - "Yes" Honorable members against this proposal say "No". The sound of "No" was not heard. Therefore, I declare that the proposal that the Nepal Special Service Act, 2042 (Amendment) Bill, 2083, sent with a message from the House of Representatives, be sent to the Legislation Management Committee for clause-by-clause discussion has been approved by consensus. Honorable members, the next meeting of the National Assembly will convene on Monday, Bhadra 16, 2083, at 1:15 PM, and this meeting is hereby adjourned. (Thereafter, this meeting was adjourned to convene on Monday, Bhadra 16, 2083, at 1:15 PM.) Adjourned: 10:35 AM.
